item.title: States Weekly Newsletter: July 22, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers July 22, 2026.

item.title: Understanding President Trump’s New Tariffs on Canadian Imports
item.description: On July 20, President Trump formally invoked Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 for the first time to impose 50 percent duties against a significant range of Canadian products. Our experts explain the statute and its global implications.

item.title: World Cup 2026: North America Missed the Goal
item.description: The 2026 World Cup presented a unique opportunity for trilateral cooperation in North America amid mounting economic and security tensions. It failed to deliver on what should have been an easy goal.

item.title: Elbows Up: The Price of Economic Coercion Against Canada
item.description: The United States has announced 50 percent tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports. If enacted, the measures would have implications for economic welfare and trade diversification in both countries.

item.title: Bolstering Pacific Resilience: A New Paradigm for Engagement by U.S. Allies and Partners
item.description: The ability to build resilience, not just security partnerships, may be the United States' greatest strategic advantage in the Pacific.

item.title: America’s Unproven Productivity Boom, and the Cost of Misreading the Data
item.description: The recent boom in U.S. labor productivity may not be early dividends of new AI technologies, but a routine labor market adjustment. Until the data starts to provide a clearer story, policymakers would be wise to consider the jury out to avoid serious policy missteps.

item.title: Is the Iran War Entering a Dangerous New Phase?
item.description: Escalating U.S.-Iran strikes are widening the conflict beyond the Strait of Hormuz, threatening Gulf infrastructure, regional stability, and global energy security. Yet behind the fighting, mediators are searching for an off-ramp before the crisis spirals further.

item.title: Ending Forced Labor: Comparing EU and U.S. Approaches
item.description: The European Union’s new Forced Labor Regulation joins U.S. import bans in targeting goods made with forced labor. The effectiveness of both approaches will depend on credible enforcement, strong due diligence and reporting mechanisms, and meaningful worker engagement.
